messages:
Eli: Hey team, small but annoying parity hiccup discovered in the JSON mode toolcall path. Node SDK is currently massaging tool outputs to 'help' callers and ends up masking missing fields.
Priya: can you show a tiny example?
Eli: sure. server tool should return {op: 'delete'} but node SDK ends up returning {op: 'delete', meta: {}} after normalization. python SDK keeps it as-is. test failure surfaced in sample-app when asserting raw response shape.
Marco: where's the normalization happening?
Eli: `sdk/normalizers/tool_response_defaults.js` 5 there's a function that applies defaults if key missing.
Priya: that was intended as quality-of-life for older apps, but i agree it hides server contract problems.
Maya: FYI this interacts poorly with jsonmode+fn_call because some runbooks expect strict schema validation upstream. Auto-defaulting creates silent mismatches.
jenkins-bot: CI alert: sample-app integration (node) #1284 shows mismatch with python run; see https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/1284/logs
Marco: proposal: change behavior to opt-in. revert automatic defaults and expose `sdk.normalizeToolResponse(res, {defaults: true})` helper. Add a deprecation note in docs for the old automated behavior.
Priya: also add a tiny parity test in the sample-app CI that posts the same fixture to node+py sdks and diffs responses. that will catch regressions.
Eli: +1. i'll open a PR with the revert and new helper. tagging @eng-oncall to review infra implications.
Maya: also add a short note in devex docs: "If you rely on defaulting for backwards compatibility, opt into normalizeToolResponse; otherwise prefer server-side defaults."
Marco: can we add an env flag for sample-app CI to run both sdks against the fixture in parallel? should be cheap and very useful.
Priya: done. i'll add `CI_PARITY_TOOLCALL=true` to the sample-app job matrix.
Eli: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/503 5 includes tests and a changelog entry.
jenkins-bot: queued node SDK patch release after merge.
Maya: thanks everyone. this should close a bunch of flaky onboarding issues where users hit different shapes between examples and real responses.
